files.generation_prompt:
Generate a new production sprite sheet. Strict camera requirement: ORTHOGRAPHIC PLAN VIEW, looking STRAIGHT DOWN, camera optical axis perpendicular to every rock's broad top surface. This must look like six top-down game tokens viewed from directly overhead. The references show angled rocks and side lighting; those aspects must NOT be reproduced. Match ONLY their material and colour. Do not copy any cyan outline from the references.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a sprite sheet of six single asteroids for the battle background of Stellar Syndicates, a dark science-fiction strategy game. The game cuts the sheet into six separate sprites and scatters them, turned to any angle and at any size, beneath a space battle.
Image 1 is the game's existing rock sprite for this belt: match its rock material, colours and finish, but draw single rocks, not clusters.
Image 2 is the game's painting of this belt: a material and colour reference only. Do not copy its scene, camera or lighting.
Composition: one landscape 1536 x 1024 canvas holding exactly six separate asteroids in a 3 x 2 grid, each centred in its own 512 x 512 cell and filling about 70% of it, with at least 60 px of clear transparent space between any two rocks. Nothing crosses a cell's edge. No grid lines, cell borders or labels.
Camera: straight top-down, looking directly down on each rock (not a three-quarter or side view), so a rock can be turned to any angle.
Lighting: soft, even light from directly above, toward the viewer. Craters and crevices sit in soft shadow and each rock's outer edge falls slightly darker. No bright side, no highlight on one edge, no rim light and no cast shadow, so a rock reads the same at any rotation.
The six rocks, left to right, top row then bottom row:
1. a long, narrow potato-shaped rock;
2. a large rounded boulder with two shallow craters;
3. an angular wedge-shaped shard with flat broken faces;
4. a lumpy two-lobed rock, two boulders fused together;
5. a flat irregular slab with a chipped edge;
6. a chunky, compact rock with jagged edges.
Rock type: Grey-brown porous stony rock with pitted surfaces, a few pale chips and small glassy olive-green olivine flecks.
Style: realistic game sprite with a crisp silhouette that reads at 30 px, natural rock detail, restrained texture, no painterly blur.
Background: genuinely transparent PNG with real RGBA alpha; no starfield, dust, glow, haze, shadow plate, ground, frame, text, labels or watermark.

Production correction: the camera has zero tilt, no perspective or foreshortening. The broad faces of the wedge and slab are parallel to the image plane; do not show a tall front wall or a tall right wall on any rock. All rocks have subtle, balanced edge shading on every side, with the brightest diffuse surface region facing the viewer at the centre, not one direction. Light comes from a large soft source exactly coaxial with the camera. No upper-left key light or lower-right dark side.

Precisely retain a 1536 x 1024 transparent canvas and a regular 3 x 2 layout. Each whole rock must fit inside a 360 x 360 box centred at (256,256), (768,256), (1280,256), (256,768), (768,768), or (1280,768), respectively. These are bounding limits, not visible boxes. Keep each natural silhouette crisp. Outside the six silhouettes, every pixel is fully transparent alpha=0: empty cutout canvas, no halo, gradients, backlighting, shadows or loose debris.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the attached sprite sheet for production. Preserve the six asteroid materials, colour palette, crisp realistic game-sprite finish, shape order and 1536 x 1024 canvas. Keep the six single rocks as long, round with two craters, wedge, fused two-lobed, slab and compact, in a 3 by 2 grid.
Correct the spacing: reduce EACH rock to about 75% of its current linear size, and centre it within its own 512 x 512 cell. Each rock's bounding box must be at most 360 pixels wide and at most 360 pixels high. Rock centres are (256,256), (768,256), (1280,256), (256,768), (768,768), (1280,768). Leave generous empty margins on every side of every cell. Keep the whole canvas uncropped.
Use a strict straight-down orthographic view and soft even light coming directly from the viewer; evenly darken the perimeter, with no bright side. The broad face of each rock faces straight towards the viewer. The wedge and slab should show their broad top footprints, with no tall front or right side walls.
True transparent RGBA output, alpha=0 outside the rock silhouettes, no halos, glow, dust, shadow or backdrop of any sort. Do not paint a replacement background. No borders, text or labels.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create a NEW 2D TOP-DOWN GAME SPRITE ATLAS for Stellar Syndicates. Image 1 supplies only the fractured-rock material. Image 2 supplies only the colour palette. Ignore all camera angles and lighting in both references.

The six sprites are overhead plan views of single asteroid fragments: their broad faces point straight at the viewer, like the terrain in a satellite orthophoto. The camera is exactly 90 degrees overhead. Render flat irregular footprints with realistic detailed rock surfaces and subtle local crack relief. Avoid extruded block shapes or thick visible front/right walls. Lighting is diffuse and coaxial with the viewer, with subtle evenly darkened edges around every side.

Rock material: naturally weathered rust-red and charcoal planetary crust, jagged fractures and visible layered strata within surface breaks, with only a FEW SMALL SUBTLE metallic veins. The rock is cold. Veins are non-emissive natural mineral traces, never yellow glowing lava or bright continuous gold networks. Crisp realistic texture, restrained detail.

1536 x 1024 PNG with genuine transparent alpha. Exactly SIX separate single rocks in a regular 3 columns x 2 rows grid. Centre each within a 512 x 512 cell. Each rock is about 320 pixels across its longest dimension, leaving VERY generous transparent space around every object. Keep all six completely inside their individual cells.
Top row: long narrow potato-shaped fragment; rounded boulder with two shallow round craters; triangular wedge-shaped shard.
Bottom row: fused two-lobed fragment; broad thin irregular slab with a chipped outline; compact chunky jagged fragment.
Pure transparent empty canvas outside the six cutout silhouettes. No background, no ground, no cast shadows, no glow or halos, no rim lights, no dust or loose debris, no text, no borders.

Preserve the exact rock designs, surface textures, rust-red and charcoal colours, subtle mineral veins, overhead viewing angles, lighting and shape order. Keep exactly the same SIX rocks. Do not redesign, brighten, relight or rotate them.
Keep the full 1536 x 1024 transparent canvas. Shrink each rock to 70% of its current width and height, then place it at the exact centre of its 512 x 512 cell in the existing 3 x 2 grid. Every rock must fit inside a 350 x 350 invisible bounding box. Keep the rest of each cell empty transparent space. Do not enlarge the rocks to fill the canvas. This edit must create noticeably wider empty margins all around every rock. No rock may cross a cell boundary.
Preserve genuine transparent RGBA output and crisp edges. Outside the six silhouettes, leave only fully transparent pixels with no backdrop, halos, glow, ground shadows or debris. Keep the sheet uncropped and untrimmed.
